donts: Don't add a box-shadow with a blur radius. The Zero Blur Rule has no exceptions, including hover, modals and anything that floats.
Don't let an application colour become a fill, a text colour, or a full border. it is a 4px top edge and a 9px dot, and that is the whole vocabulary.
Don't render a zero count as 0. it is an em dash in Ink Faint; a blue nought claims a measurement that never happened.
Don't reflow the board at narrow widths. it scrolls horizontally inside its container, because a rewrapped keyboard is not a keyboard.
Don't introduce a spacing step larger than 22px. this page is dense on purpose and a wide gap reads as a missing section.
Don't animate anything. there is no motion vocabulary here and adding one would be a new world, not a refinement.
dos: Do keep every new surface inside the three-step tonal stack — Desk, Deck, Cap. a fourth tone has to displace one of them, not join them.
Do give a number tabular-nums whenever it can be compared to the number above it.
Do write the empty state as a bare fact in Ink Faint, in the same grid as the rows it replaces, so the column does not jump when data arrives.
Do use mono for a chord and sans for a sentence, without exception.
Do keep the accent to chosen, pressed and annotated. a fourth use has to retire one.
keyCharacteristics: zero blur anywhere; depth is tonal stacking plus one 2px physical lip
two type families split by gesture: mono for what you type, sans for what you read
colour is a label, never a decoration — eight app hues and one accent, nothing else
flat, bright, and legible at a glance; no gradients, no glass, no animation
narrative.overview:
the system draws a keyboard as a keyboard. its one structural decision is a box-shadow with a blur radius of zero — 0 2px 0 in the cap-edge grey — which is not a shadow at all but the lip of a moulded key seen straight on. every other decision follows from that literalism.

the register is quiet on purpose. a key is grey until something is bound to it, plain until it has been pressed, and coloured only to say which application owns it. nothing on the page is decorated; every mark is a fact that was measured on this machine.

density is high and unapologetic, because the whole board has to be legible in one glance, without scrolling, at the moment a decision is being made.

rules.body: an application's colour appears only as a bound key's 4px top edge and its 9px list dot. never a fill, never text, never a border on more than one side.
rules.name: The Owner Edge Rule

rules.body: Signal Blue marks exactly three states — chosen, pressed, annotated. a count of zero renders as an em dash in Ink Faint, not a blue nought.
rules.name: The Earned Accent Rule

rules.body: mono for anything you could type; sans for anything you only read. a chord is always mono, a sentence is never.
rules.name: The Two Hands Rule

rules.body: every number that can be compared to another number carries tabular-nums. a column that jitters cannot be scanned.
rules.name: The Tabular Rule

rules.body: no box-shadow in this system carries a blur radius. not on hover, not on a dialog, not on a dropdown that does not exist yet.
rules.name: The Zero Blur Rule

rules.body: a bound key nobody has pressed is outlined, not greyed. it is not disabled and it is not an error — it is a question about why the binding exists.
rules.name: The Cold Ring Rule
